observations.title: Pelorus Reef volcano (Tonga)
observations.description: The Tonga Geological Services (TGS) reported new eruptive activity at Pelorus Reef, previously referred to as Volcano 8 (cruise designation) or Tofua Arc at 22.8°S (arc location), during 13-16 November. Thermal anomalies were identified in satellite images on 13 and 15 November, rising steam plumes were visible in a 14 November image, and discolored water and floating pumice rafts were identified in images during 14-16 November. Underwater sound signals in the area were interpreted as high-frequency underwater volcanic explosions. The Laboratoire de Géophysique de Tahiti analyzed satellite observations and acoustic data and reported additional details. A volcanic cloud, 42 km in diameter, was visible at 1300 on 13 November. On 14 November two pumice rafts, 13 km and 21 km long, were located around the emission point. An area of discolored water that was 931 square kilometers was also observed on that same day. Explosive hydroacoustic activity was detected from 1049 on 15 November to 0642 on 18 November by the Laboratoire de Géophysique de Tahiti seismic network in French Polynesia. A total of 300 hydroacoustic explosions were detected and located at 22.64°S, 175.66°W, near Pelorus Reef. The strongest explosion was recorded at 2036 on 15 on November. Pelorus Reef is described as a large submerged Pleistocene caldera system located about 60 km SSW of Ata Island, 217 km SW of 'Eua Island, and 220 km SW of Tongatapu Island. The W part of the caldera rim was about 35 m below sea level. There are no known Holocene eruptions, prior to the current activity. Sources: Laboratoire de Géophysique de Tahiti,Tonga Geological Services, Government of Tonga
